newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mostly steady.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady with a negative bias on Thursday despite the run-up in CBOT grain and oilseed markets, dealers said.
"Demand wise, the fundamentals in millfeeds have not changed from a day or two ago. We are seeing some weakness creeping in," a Buffalo dealer said.
He said he believed the rally in soybeans and wheat will support the markets in Kansas. "They seem to like to trade midds off what the board is doing," he said.
Another dealer said he believed midds will not price themselves out of the market as a result of the bean rally.
"One thing about millfeed is that it gets sold. It is kind of an auction market," he said. "If they have to be $6 cheaper to trade, then they will be $6 cheaper to trade."
But one broker said if midds become too high, substitutes such as soy hulls would more attractive. "Soy hulls are very reasonable," he said.
Feed business was already affected by the emergence of spring as livestock begins feeding on grass in Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas, a Kansas dealer said.

"Demand has fallen off on these midds because of the pastures out here in the Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas markets," he said. "There will be plenty of midds. Cattle are already feeding on pasture," he said.
The action on the CBOT board was trying to be "friendly" to midds, a Carolinas dealer said.
But he noted other cheaper products such as hominy and soy hulls were working there way into the market. "So we are starting to see those trade now as replacements," he said.
He noted flour mill run times were still slow and as the Easter holiday nears, dealers were anticipating next week to be a short week, which would keep prices firm.
